qualifying_findings.title: Model artifact and configuration loading code-execution cluster
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records code-injection or unsafe-deserialization paths in ModelTC LightX2V tokenizer auto_map loading, RAE config-driven model instantiation, yolov13 AutoBackend model metadata, TensorLayer HDF5 graph loading, and ComfyUI Segment Anything GroundingDINO config loading. Several records state that public exploit information exists and lack a vendor-confirmed patched version.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE records; in-window publication or update; model artifact and configuration supply-chain compromise surface
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: LightX2V through 0.5.0; RAE through commit a4d18c4; yolov13 through commit 7328994; TensorLayer through 2.2.4; comfyui_segment_anything through commit ab63955.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model packages, tokenizer metadata, and configuration files must be treated as executable supply-chain inputs; provenance, isolation, and artifact validation gates are required before loading them.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad framework and model-loader catalog context is upstream-owned.
Unsafe artifact/configuration loading and supply-chain controls are local security concerns.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in NVD timing and affected-boundary summaries; ingest should reconcile each rolling-release fix with repository commits or vendor releases.

qualifying_findings.title: Model-loader malformed-artifact memory-safety cluster
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Recent NVD records describe remotely triggerable malformed-model or model-metadata handling flaws: sherpa-onnx vocabulary metadata buffer overflow, PowerInfer GGUF offset out-of-bounds read, OAID Tengine tmfile offset out-of-bounds read, and Praat's embedded whisper.cpp model dimension out-of-bounds write. Praat identifies patch a910d21 and version 7.0.03 as an initial remediation.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE records; in-window publication or update; model-runtime artifact parsing weaknesses
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: sherpa-onnx through 1.13.8; PowerInfer through commit 8bd56d6; Tengine through 1.12.0; Praat through 7.0.02 / embedded whisper.cpp model loader.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted weights and model packs cross a high-risk native parsing boundary. Model distribution controls should include integrity verification, sandboxed conversion/loading, and prompt incident patch triage.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad model runtime and artifact-format context belongs upstream.
Artifact parsing attack surface, mitigation, and release-gate implications are local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in published NVD descriptions; fixed-version and reachability claims need primary repository validation during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: obsidian-tc resolved-path ACL and bridge-field disclosure fixes
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: obsidian-tc before 1.3.1 applied read ACL checks to lexical vault-relative paths while containment used resolved paths, enabling an in-vault symlink to expose denied files. Separate bridge tools leaked ACL-protected derived fields or template paths and function bodies. Version 1.3.1 applies ACL filtering to resolved paths and relevant returned fields.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE records; in-window publication; agent-ready local knowledge-server authorization fix
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: obsidian-tc before 1.3.1; vault read ACL, bridge-tool return-field, and template enumeration boundaries
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool authorization must apply after canonicalization and to every response field; agent-accessible local knowledge can otherwise leak beyond the caller's intended context scope.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Obsidian and MCP-server context is upstream-owned.
ACL canonicalization and tool-output disclosure are local security boundaries.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD publication and explicit fixed version; check the 1.3.1 release notes during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: Kubeflow Model Registry annotation SSRF and controller-token exposure
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Kubeflow Model Registry through 0.3.17 allows namespace users to point the modelregistry.kubeflow.org/url annotation at an attacker server. The NVD record says this can capture the controller ServiceAccount bearer token and enable modification of other tenants' InferenceServices cluster-wide.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record; in-window publication; cloud model-registry SSRF and workload-identity exposure
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Model Registry through 0.3.17; InferenceService annotation URL and controller ServiceAccount token boundary
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model registry metadata must not be able to exfiltrate workload credentials; this is a direct AI deployment-plane least-privilege and egress-control failure.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Kubeflow product background is upstream-owned.
Cloud deployment credential and SSRF boundary belongs locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in NVD timing and impact statement; ingest should locate the upstream Kubeflow patch/advisory for remediation specifics.

qualifying_findings.title: Ludwig dataset archive symlink extraction escape
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Ludwig before 0.17.8 validates tar member names but not symlink or hard-link entries before extraction, so a crafted dataset archive can write through a link outside the extraction directory. NVD also notes an os.path.commonprefix containment weakness and states 0.17.8 fixes the issue; Python 3.14's default tar data filter is not affected.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE record; in-window publication; dataset supply-chain path traversal
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Ludwig before 0.17.8; configured archive URL / dataset extraction boundary on Python 3.12 and 3.13
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Training and evaluation dataset intake can become arbitrary host writes when archive provenance or extraction isolation is weak.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Ludwig framework context is upstream-owned.
Dataset intake and extraction controls are local supply-chain concerns.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence; version and Python-runtime conditions are directly stated in NVD.

qualifying_findings.title: Official MCP Java and Python HTTP request-size exhaustion fixes
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD documents three availability controls for official MCP SDK Streamable HTTP deployments: Java SDK transports through mcp-core 2.0.0 read unbounded request bodies (fixed 0.18.4, 1.1.4, 2.0.1); Python SDK HTTP/session/OAuth routes buffer full bodies (fixed 1.29.1 and 2.1.0); and stateful Python SDK sessions can accumulate without expiry or aggregate limits (fixed 1.30.0 and 2.2.0).
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD/CVE records; in-window publication; official MCP SDK transport availability and resource-control fixes
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MCP Java SDK 0.8.0 through 2.0.0 depending on artifact line; MCP Python SDK pre-1.29.1 / 2.0.0a1 through 2.0.1; stateful Python sessions through 1.30.0 / 2.2.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Public or broadly reachable MCP HTTP transports need explicit request-size, concurrency, session TTL, and upstream-proxy limits even where authentication exists.

upstream_routing.reason: MCP SDK catalog and protocol background are upstream-owned.
Transport exposure, resource limits, and patch gates are local security controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in NVD patch lines; ingest should verify each affected range against primary release advisories.
